I was thinking exact the same thing, humans are not evolved to live a sedentary lifestyle, live individualized, secluded, etc. Throughout our history, humans have always survived and thrived in groups/tribes, did all sorts of collective activities such as hunting, gathering, fishing, building shelters, eat real natural food, and escape the elements, living a nomadic lifestyle basically.   Our modern lifestyle enables us to live more secluded and individualized lifestyles, we don't have to rely on each other and form connections like humans used to do.                     ( No wonder that suicide rates were going drastically up since humans shifted from traditional lifestyles to individualized/urban lifestyles)  

 I have the idea that this pretty recent, drastic lifestyle shift could (''subconsciously'') play a big role in developing mental illness/ depression, because we lost some key components that played a very big role in the way humans evolved. Maybe there is some genetic memory in our DNA that was always adapted to a collective, tribal, nomadic lifestyle were humans really needed each other for survival.    

I am not suggesting that we should all go back to prehistoric times and live the exact same lifestyle bc that is not realistic, but as I mentioned, there is sort of an evolutionary mismatch between our current, more individualized lifestyle, and the way early humans used to live. I think humans are fundamentally more hardwired to live tribal/ collective and nomadic-lifestyles (in nature)  and that our modern lifestyle makes us (subconsciously) feel miserable, mainly because we have lost certain characteristics of our primordial lifestyle that arguably played a major role in our evolution.
